output.summary: Revision 2 adopts G1038 §6 verbatim: G1039 only replaces the body of carry.unchanged(ident, node, key, old_cp, new_cp, scope) with a zero-context patch-id comparison (Identity.change gains unified=; the scope is records.checkpoint_scope from record.frozen, never stored; carry.relocate and the kept change are G1038's), and the sync card reads synced = {old, onto, work, tip, merge, resolved} while previous.interdiff/previous.syncs stay G1038's. In rebase mode (until the policy requires merge_sync) carry stays today's replay map, but the review_impl base edge, the sync-focused card and the budget exemption still apply; sticky merge mode keeps the widened predicate on merge-synced branches only. round_budget is checked against G1027's merged capability code: one file under engine/capabilities/, appended to SHIPPED, and the new counting rule is used only while the policy requires it (SPEC §4.5). The budget redefinition (10 rounds with new material findings per stage) is unchanged.

findings.text: Clean-sync predicate: the -U0 patch id ignores position. With identity.py's DIFF flags at --unified=0 and patch-id --verbatim, the same goal line inserted after line 10 and after line 30 gives an identical id (1b4a7646dfe2 both times; the -U3 ids differ). §3.1 leaves synced.resolved out of the predicate and claims that equal -U0 ids mean 'exactly new trunk plus the goal's own lines'. That is false for hand-resolved files: keeping both sides in a different order, moving the goal's lines elsewhere in the file, or deleting the wrong copy of a duplicated line all keep the id. test_design is then carried and review_tests is skipped although the tests' meaning changed, which contradicts the spec ('conflict resolutions ... stale as today'). A trunk-only merge cannot move goal lines, so the gap is limited to synced.resolved. Fix: for each path in synced.resolved inside the node's scope, also require a position-aware check, for example that the resolved blob equals `git merge-file -p --union` of the B0/onto/tip versions in either side order (this still carries the HISTORY both-rows case); otherwise the node stales. Add tests for a reordered both-sides code resolution and for a moved goal line. Also align §1 ('trunk edits inside the goal's hunks' stale) with test 4, which carries context edits inside the -U3 hunk: say 'trunk edits to the goal's own -/+ lines'.

Sync card size: §3.4 says that over 4,096 bytes 'G1018's shrink steps blob sync.touching', but at f4eaf74 card._steps (and the SPEC §4.20 list) only blobs prompt, instructions, inputs/context/policy, corrections, candidates and notes, so a new top-level `sync` key is never shrunk. Real review_impl re-run cards are already at or over the target because `previous` is never shrunk (G1022 review_impl attempt 2 is about 4.0 KB, G1027 review_impl attempt 2 about 5.6 KB). Adding about 1.3 KB of inline sync, including a roughly 550-byte constant ask, makes about 7 KB. Test 11 ('at most 4,096 bytes after shrink, at real sizes') cannot hold, and it conflicts with test_a_card_over_budget_because_of_previous_is_a_fixed_point. Fix: specify new shrink steps in SPEC §4.20 and card.py (blob sync.touching, keeping more/all, then the rest of sync except from/to/diff/log) and list them in the §4 table. Consider moving the constant ask into review_impl's prompt or a fixed blob. Restate test 11 as a bound on what sync adds after shrink, plus the fixed point for a card over the target because of previous.

Budget exemption is too broad: §3.5 exempts any record that started stale with all of its stale keys being inputs selecting a git.base node, and calls this 'exactly the clean-sync review_impl re-run'. But test_design and implement also take base.base_commit as a non-context input. When carry rejects them (the sync was not clean for them), they re-run stale only on inputs.base and are exempt. They do raise new material findings (G1027 implement:1:1, G1026 test_design:1:1), and such a round is not caused by a clean sync. Fix: also require that the node has no checkpoint outputs (a checkpointing node stale only on base is one that carry refused), so in practice only review nodes whose subject was carried are exempt. Add a counts() row: implement stale only on inputs.base after a refused carry, raising a new material finding, counts 1.

output.summary: Changes requested. The split with G1038 is right: §6 is adopted faithfully, with no duplicated carry or relocation work. Rebase mode and the round_budget gating match the merged G1027 code. The G1026 and G1027 budget replays (3/4 and 1/4) check out against the goal refs. Three defects remain. (1) The -U0 patch id ignores position (checked: the same line inserted at line 10 or line 30 gives the same id), so a hand resolution that reorders or moves the goal's lines passes as clean and review_tests is skipped. (2) No shrink step reaches the new top-level `sync` card section, and re-run review_impl cards are already 4.0-5.6 KB, so test 11 cannot hold. (3) The budget exemption also matches test_design and implement re-runs after a non-clean sync.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1. Every sync of a goal with the integration branch marks test_design, review_tests, implement, run_tests and review_impl stale, even when the goal's own diff did not change. G1027 synced twice and ran out of its correction budget (19 of 18) mostly that way.

Owner decisions (verbatim):
- "Ok I guess, but syncing to trunk changes things semantically like you said."
- On what re-runs after a sync merge where the goal's own diff didn't change, the owner chose "Tests + code review": design and tests reviews stay valid; run_tests always re-runs, and review_impl re-runs with a card focused on what the trunk merge brought in.
- "I think we may as well get these done now, before dogfooding again"

Scope:
- A sync whose goal diff is unchanged (the goal's own changes against the new trunk equal its changes against the old trunk, apart from context) keeps design, review_design, approve_design, test_design, review_tests and implement current.
- run_tests always re-runs after a sync.
- review_impl re-runs after a sync; its card shows what the trunk brought in that touches the goal (files the goal also changes, names it uses) and asks for semantic conflicts, not a full re-review.
- A sync that changes the goal's diff (conflict resolutions, or trunk changes inside the goal's hunks) stales as today.
- Re-runs caused by a clean sync do not count against the goal's correction budget.

Budget redefinition (owner: "Ok go with the recommendation", answering "why does a goal even _need_ a correction budget?"):
- The budget's job is to catch reviews that never converge (a new material finding every round, so no single finding repeats and no dispute fires). Today it counts every correction run, and its only firing in the Release 1 run (G1027, 19 of 18) was a false positive caused by syncs and reorder resubmits.
- Redefine it as a limit on review rounds per stage that raise new material findings. Re-runs after a clean sync, resubmits that only carry findings forward, and run_tests reruns do not count.
- Default about 10 such rounds per stage (G1026's design took 7 to 8 real rounds). Reaching it asks the owner, as today, to continue, hold or cancel.
- Acceptance adds: replaying G1027 does not reach the budget; replaying G1026's design rounds counts only rounds with new material findings.

Acceptance:
- Replaying G1027's second sync (onto G1022) keeps the reviews of design and tests, re-runs run_tests, and gives review_impl a sync-focused card that names the graph26 fixture change.
- A conflicting sync stales as today.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes and adds a HISTORY §4 row.
title: A clean trunk sync keeps design and tests reviews; run_tests and a focused code review re-run
